html:
A kingdom based in the Punjab, created by Ranjit Singh when he took Lahore in 1799, and annexed by the British in 1849 after two wars. It was the last major region of the subcontinent to fall to British rule.

In the 1700s the Sikhs, followers of the faith founded by Guru Nanak, had fought off Mughal governors and Afghan invasions and organised themselves into a dozen bands called misls. Ranjit Singh, leader of one of them, united the rest by war and marriage. He was proclaimed Maharaja in 1801.

His conquests:

  • Amritsar in 1802,
  • Multan in 1818,
  • Kashmir in 1819,
  • Peshawar, taken from the Afghan Durrani kingdom, in 1834.

In 1809 he agreed with the British to keep to the north of the Sutlej river, and he kept that peace all his life. He built a modern army, drilled by European officers who had served Napoleon, with strong artillery. Though a devout Sikh, he employed Muslims and Hindus in high office. He covered the Harmandir Sahib at Amritsar in gilded copper, which gave it its English name, the Golden Temple. He also owned the Koh-i-Noor diamond.

After he died in 1839, his heirs were murdered one after another and the army grew unruly. The East India Company won the First Anglo-Sikh War in 1845 and 1846 and the Second in 1848 and 1849, and annexed the Punjab. The boy king Duleep Singh was taken to England, and the Koh-i-Noor was given to Queen Victoria.
